title: Nubank Secures Brazil Banking License to Save Its Iconic Name
summary: The neobank, which also runs a crypto business, received approval to purchase Banco Porto Real de Investimentos S/A, becoming a licensed bank in Brazil. The development enables the company to maintain its name, as regulators pressured it to drop the bank moniker since it was not licensed as a bank i...
content:
1. News
  2. Finance
  3. Nubank Secures Brazil Banking License to Save Its Iconic Name

Published:Nov 14, 2026, 10:10 PM EST

The neobank, which also runs a crypto business, received approval to purchase Banco Porto Real de Investimentos S/A, becoming a licensed bank in Brazil. The development enables the company to maintain its name, as regulators pressured it to drop the bank moniker since it was not licensed as a bank in the country.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 14, 2026, 10:10 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Nubank secured a Brazilian banking license, allowing it to legally keep its name under new regulations.
  • The license solidifies its dominance in Brazil, where it invested $7.9B and serves 65% of adults.
  • Nubank also expanded to the US and launched Nu Global, a USDC account for cross-border crypto payments.

Nubank Receives Banking License in Brazil Through Acquisition

Nubank, one of the largest digital banks in Latam, is ready to become a bank in Brazil, its largest market in the region.

The company, with 120 million customers in Brazil and 140 million across all markets, has announced that it received approval from the Central Bank of Brazil to complete the acquisition of Banco Porto Real de Investimentos S/A, a transaction announced in July. The transaction allows Nubank to deal with a pending compliance issue regarding Joint Resolution No. 17, issued on November 28, 2025, by the Central Bank and the National Monetary Council

The resolution establishes that financial institutions must use terms that clearly inform about the type of business they conduct and the services they offer, avoiding names suggesting activities they aren’t authorized to conduct to reinforce market transparency and avoid misleading consumers.

Consequently, the company can maintain its Nubank name, adding the banking license to its payment institution, credit, financing, investment, and securities brokerage activities while complying with fintech regulations in the country.

Livia Chanes, CEO of Nubank for Brazil and Latin America, stressed the relevance of receiving this license for the company.

“Trust is built on transparency and respect for the people who choose Nubank. The banking license continues that path and reinforces our commitment to those who stand by us and to the national financial system,” she declared.

Brazil is Nubank’s main market, where the company has recently invested 45 billion reais ($7.9 billion), reaching 1 in every 5 adults and allowing them to have access to account credit and crypto investments via its app.

During its Q3 financial results, Nubank disclosed that it serves 65% of the adult population, with activity rising for the seventh consecutive quarter to a record 86.3% in Brazil.

In September, the company announced an expansion into the U.S. after receiving conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January, partnering with Kansas City-based Lead Bank to offer its services under a bank partner model.

Leveraging its presence in these jurisdictions, Nubank launched Nu Global, a USDC-based account that allows users to move money across borders and pay with crypto with an associated credit card. “We want to earn the place of being people’s primary banking relationship, and capturing even a small share of the U.S. market will be transformative for our business,” said Cristina Junqueira, co-founder and CEO of Nu U.S.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: DOJ Secures Court Approval Targeting $1.2B in Stolen Binance Crypto
summary: The Justice Department secured court authorization targeting more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance. The action formed part of a recovery effort that froze billions of dollars following an attack U.S. authorities attributed to North Korea. Court Orders Target More Than $1.2 Bil...
content:
The Justice Department secured court authorization targeting more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance. The action formed part of a recovery effort that froze billions of dollars following an attack U.S. authorities attributed to North Korea.

Key Takeaways

  • Government and private-sector efforts froze more than $2.7 billion.
  • The theft exceeded $6 billion, U.S. authorities said.
  • Launderers moved stolen assets through nearly 27,000 wallets.

Court Orders Target More Than $1.2 Billion

The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) announced on Nov. 12 that it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain stolen Binance assets worth more than $1.2 billion. Those funds were part of more than $2.7 billion frozen through coordinated government and private-sector efforts. The department attributed the theft of more than $6 billion around Oct. 29 to North Korean military hackers.

Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor said:

“The National Security Division will use every tool at its disposal to seize and return North Korea’s ill-gotten gains.”

The department linked North Korea’s cryptocurrency thefts to financing its government and illicit weapons program. Seizure places assets under government custody or control; restraint restricts their transfer while proceedings continue.

The same Nov. 12 announcement also covered Facestealer, a separate North Korean scheme that used secretly recorded videos and deepfakes to target people in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors. According to the DOJ, the scheme stole more than $400 million over 18 months, and the FBI seized cloud infrastructure behind it and more than 900 webcam videos of victims.

Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of affected assets after committing more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses. The exchange also published a reserve snapshot covering 198 tokens. It captured balances at midnight UTC that day.

FBI Sought Blocks on Theft-Linked Transactions

In an Oct. 31 alert, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed the Binance theft to Tradertraitor, its designation for the North Korean hacking activity. Working with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, the bureau observed attackers converting stolen assets primarily into ether. It expected further laundering through decentralized finance and instant-swap services, which exchange one cryptocurrency for another.

Authorities urged exchanges, infrastructure operators, and other digital asset businesses to block transactions involving or derived from identified addresses. North Korea denied responsibility for the Binance hack on Nov. 3. Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, rejected the FBI’s attribution in a statement carried by state media.

Investigators were pursuing funds moving through bridges that transfer assets between blockchains, mixers, and exchanges, according to the DOJ. The department said tracing, freezing, seizure, and forfeiture work remained underway as the attackers continued laundering the assets.

Laundering Network Complicates Recovery

Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, which traces cryptocurrency transactions to identify illicit activity, tracked conversions of stolen solana, XRP, and tron into bitcoin. Its Nov. 13 update counted nearly 27,000 wallets, at least 16 blockchains, at least 36 services, and more than 83,000 transactions across the laundering operation.

The firm also identified meme coins used to disguise Binance theft proceeds on Tron, Solana, and Near. Newly created tokens featured in the Tron and Near activity, while the Solana tactic involved existing assets. Trading through token liquidity pools allowed stolen funds to pass between wallets without a direct transfer linking the sender and recipient.

Elliptic’s update covering Nov. 11-13 described light activity beyond further XRP swaps. Converted proceeds had reached roughly 4,100 bitcoin, valued at $285 million at the time. Its mixing estimates included roughly 11,000 ether in laundering-linked deposits into Tornado Cash.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $2.35 Billion in Two Weeks as BlackRock’s Outflow Streak Hits 11
summary: Two consecutive billion-dollar outflow weeks leave Bitcoin’s institutional demand under pressure. BlackRock’s IBIT accounts for most of the latest withdrawals, but the numbers need careful reading.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Two consecutive billion-dollar outflow weeks leave Bitcoin’s institutional demand under pressure. BlackRock’s IBIT accounts for most of the latest withdrawals, but the numbers need careful reading.

Bitcoin ETF outflows have reached $2.347 billion across the first two completed November trading weeks, leaving a persistent hole in one of the market’s most closely watched sources of demand.

BNC’s calculations from Farside Investors’ fund-flow table show $1.0653 billion leaving U.S. spot Bitcoin funds during November 9–13, following $1.2817 billion in the preceding week. BlackRock’s IBIT recorded withdrawals on every session in both weeks and on October 30, extending its losing streak to 11 trading days.

The figures describe net investor flows through the products. They do not mean BlackRock’s corporate treasury has decided to sell its own Bitcoin holdings, or establish that every departing investor has abandoned cryptocurrency altogether.

Bitcoin ETF outflows remain concentrated in IBIT

IBIT accounted for $908.4 million of the latest week’s net withdrawals, about 85% of the industry total. Its November withdrawals through Friday reached $2.118 billion, approximately 90% of the combined net outflow across the funds.

Concentration matters when interpreting the headline. One very large product can drive the aggregate even while some competing funds attract money. An industry total does not show that every provider or customer group is moving in the same direction.

Friday’s $185.4 million net withdrawal was smaller than Thursday’s $284.1 million. But a less negative session remains a negative session. It is evidence that the pace changed, rather than confirmation that demand has recovered.

The industry’s losing run is shorter than IBIT’s: seven sessions, beginning November 5. On November 4, the combined funds attracted $74.6 million even as IBIT lost money. That is a concrete example of why a fund-specific streak and an industry-wide streak should not be used interchangeably. The totals here use the table as checked on November 15; automated flow datasets can subsequently be revised.

A large fund is still a large fund

The iShares product page reported IBIT net assets of approximately $54.13 billion as of November 13. Its net asset value was $39.00 per share, while its closing market price was $38.94.

Those figures put the withdrawals beside a substantial remaining investor base. They also illustrate why assets under management and fund flows should not be treated as interchangeable: assets can shrink because Bitcoin falls, because investors redeem shares, or through a combination of both.

Likewise, trading volume in ETF shares is not automatically a net inflow. Shares can change hands between buyers and sellers on an exchange without the product receiving an equivalent amount of new capital. That distinction becomes particularly useful during volatile sessions.

Reading the market therefore requires separate questions: how much exposure investors retain, how much new money enters or leaves, and how the underlying asset is priced. One dramatic number cannot answer all three.

BlackRock’s longer-term argument faces a near-term test

BlackRock has previously argued that weak flows do not necessarily overturn Bitcoin’s long-term investment case. In an earlier research paper using data through mid-2026, its digital-assets team described the pullback’s pressures as “cyclical flow dynamics.”

The paper, co-authored by Robert Mitchnick, Will Su and Alice Wang, separated episodes of leveraged selling and slowing institutional demand from its case for Bitcoin as a longer-term portfolio diversifier. It also discussed competition for capital from AI-themed investments.

That research predates the November withdrawals. It should be read as the manager’s investment framework, not a fresh explanation of this particular week. BlackRock also sponsors IBIT, giving readers a reason to distinguish its commercial perspective from the independently tabulated flows.

The tension is useful rather than contradictory. A long-term thesis can remain intact in an investor’s view while near-term allocations decline. The practical test is whether that conviction eventually translates into renewed purchases.

The macro backdrop adds another hurdle

BNC’s analysis of the latest wholesale inflation release examined the distinction between a slower monthly increase and persistent annual price pressure. For Bitcoin, the relevant channel is how that evidence influences financing conditions and willingness to hold risk.

The ETF figures cannot isolate inflation, sentiment or any other single cause of redemptions. Nor do they reveal whether investors are reducing leverage, changing vehicles, raising cash or making a permanent allocation decision. Those explanations require evidence beyond the daily totals.

What would signal a more durable improvement?

The next useful development would be sustained net buying across several sessions, ideally involving more than one fund. A single positive day could interrupt a streak without changing the wider demand picture.

It would also help to compare fund flows with spot trading and derivatives positioning over matching dates. A weekend Bitcoin move takes place while U.S. fund shares are not in their normal trading session; it should not be described as a new daily ETF-flow reading.

For now, the completed-week data show repeated withdrawals from a major access route into Bitcoin. The important question for the next trading week is whether that drain slows convincingly—and whether buyers return in sufficient size to turn stabilisation into fresh demand.

title: Bitcoin Faces Massive Liquidation Cluster Near $60K, Glassnode Warns
summary: Bitcoin approached a large concentration of leveraged trades as Glassnode warned that forced selling could deepen its decline. The warning came as shrinking trading liquidity and losses on bullish bets increased pressure across crypto markets. Glassnode Warns of Vulnerable Trades Below Bitcoin’s Pri...
content:
Bitcoin approached a large concentration of leveraged trades as Glassnode warned that forced selling could deepen its decline. The warning came as shrinking trading liquidity and losses on bullish bets increased pressure across crypto markets.

Key Takeaways

  • Glassnode identified a liquidation zone between $59,500 and $62,600.
  • Crypto liquidations reached $1.64 billion around the Nov. 13 decline.
  • Stablecoin supply contracted by $17 billion over a month.

Glassnode Warns of Vulnerable Trades Below Bitcoin’s Price

Glassnode, a firm that analyzes public blockchain data and crypto markets, issued a warning about concentrated long positions on Nov. 14. These bullish trades seek to profit from rising prices, and their liquidation cluster marks a zone where many could be forcibly closed. The firm stated:

“BTC price is approaching a massive liquidation cluster. The August breakout left behind these long entries. Markets tend to gravitate toward spots of fragility such as this. After weeks of selling, this could be the accelerant for a final capitulation flush.”

Glassnode’s Nov. 11 analysis placed the largest modeled liquidation cluster between $59,500 and $62,600 on a six-month heatmap, which uses brighter colors to indicate heavier concentrations of potential futures closures. That zone had remained untouched since the August low, while the breakout that month left those long entries, or opening points for bullish trades, in place. A capitulation flush would describe a burst of selling as traders abandon their bets under pressure.

As of 5:51 p.m. EST on Nov. 14, bitcoin traded at $63,602, down 6.90%, or $4,714.58, over 24 hours. The price was down 14.81% over one week and 21.45% over one month. Its one-year decline stood at 31.70%.

Forced Closures Meet Shrinking Trading Liquidity

Leverage lets traders control exposure larger than the funds committed, with collateral serving as backing for their trades. When losses leave too little margin to meet an exchange’s minimum requirement for keeping a trade open, the platform can trigger liquidations of bullish futures positions. Those closures can add selling pressure, particularly when many trades reach their thresholds together.

Broader strains in crypto liquidity and derivatives positioning included approximately $1.64 billion in liquidations during a 24-hour period surrounding the Nov. 13 decline, nearly 90% involving bullish trades. Liquidity describes the market’s ability to absorb transactions without large price changes, while derivatives positioning measures exposure through contracts tied to underlying assets. By Nov. 14, Glassnode also reported that stablecoin supply had contracted by $17 billion over a month, reducing capital available within crypto markets.

U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $185.4 million in net outflows on Nov. 13, including $143.5 million from Blackrock and $41.9 million from Fidelity. Withdrawals totaled approximately $1.07 billion during Nov. 9-13, with every session ending negative. Nov. 13 marked the seventh consecutive trading day of net outflows, extending the streak that began Nov. 5.

Selective Buying Offers a Counterpoint to Selling

Earlier liquidation rounds had already cleared many long positions built up during the decline from September, Glassnode noted on Nov. 11. That reduced the concentration of vulnerable trades near the price prevailing when the analysis was published. The deeper August cluster remained, creating a distinction between leverage already removed and exposure still vulnerable below the market.

Despite the decline, Glassnode’s Nov. 11 assessment of weakening demand and selective accumulation showed renewed buying among wallets holding 100 to 1,000 BTC and 1,000 to 10,000 BTC. These cohorts group wallet addresses by balance, and accumulation describes increases in their holdings. Smaller holders and the largest cohort continued reducing balances, leaving buying concentrated among selected groups.

Meanwhile, expectations of higher U.S. interest rates added to the financial backdrop. CME Fedwatch, which estimates Federal Reserve decision probabilities from futures prices, assigned an 88.5% probability to a quarter-point increase and 11.5% to a half-point move on Nov. 14. The Fed’s policy meeting was scheduled for Dec. 8-9.

title: Elon Musk Backs Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return as 120K Sign Petition
summary: Over 120,000 names appeared on a petition backed by Elon Musk seeking Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The tally included more than 6,000 self-identified current employees, while Musk warned that Huang’s departure would cost Nvidia critical supply-chain deals. Musk-Backed Petition Draws Employee...
content:
Over 120,000 names appeared on a petition backed by Elon Musk seeking Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. The tally included more than 6,000 self-identified current employees, while Musk warned that Huang’s departure would cost Nvidia critical supply-chain deals.

Key Takeaways

  • More than 65,000 signers identified themselves as Nvidia shareholders.
  • Signers included over 6,000 self-identified current employees and more than 1,100 former employees.
  • Musk warned that Huang’s departure would cost Nvidia critical deals.

Musk-Backed Petition Draws Employees and Shareholders

Stand With Jensen, a petition backed by Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk seeking Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive of Nvidia Corp. (Nasdaq: NVDA), had reached more than 120,000 names by Nov. 14. Its campaign for Huang’s reinstatement listed more than 6,000 current employees, over 1,100 former employees, more than 65,000 shareholders, and over 47,000 other supporters. Those affiliations were self-reported and unverified.

Musk said on Nov. 13 that he was signing a petition supporting Huang’s return. Replying to another user on X, he backed Huang’s reinstatement, stating: “A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.”

In a further statement on X on Nov. 14, Musk stated:

“Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia, but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract. Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.”

Campaign Demands Reinstatement and a Fair Hearing

The independent volunteer campaign demanded reinstatement, an independent investigation and fair hearing, and a timely public explanation. Organizers asked directors to provide evidence supporting Huang’s continued absence if they considered it necessary. The effort operated independently of Nvidia.

Beyond restoring Huang, the campaign sought disclosure of the inquiry’s scope, independence, and expected timeline, along with a meaningful opportunity for him to respond. Directors were also asked to explain their concerns, supporting evidence, and consideration of employee and shareholder interests. Acknowledging that they lacked access to private board deliberations, the authors said they had not been shown evidence substantiating the espionage allegation.

Public support from Musk preceded the resignation announcement. During the developing controversy, he agreed that Huang was irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership. The co-founder had led Nvidia for 33 years.

Separately, the billionaire indicated that hiring Huang would be an honor when another user suggested recruiting him. That response came before the leadership change, as uncertainty grew over whether Huang would remain in charge.

Directors Back Interim Leadership During Search

Nvidia announced Huang’s resignation on Nov. 12, covering his president, CEO, and board positions. Finance chief Colette Kress became interim CEO while retaining her financial responsibilities. Directors said they expected operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap to continue without interruption.

Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao also criticized Nvidia for letting Huang resign amid reports of affairs and allegations that foreign intelligence operatives targeted him. The board retained outside lawyers to conduct its independent inquiry: Joon H. Kim, a former top federal prosecutor for the Southern District of New York, and his law firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

Earlier leadership uncertainty also reached prediction markets, where traders bought contracts tied to Huang’s potential departure. Before the resignation announcement, Polymarket odds of him leaving by year-end reached 90.5%.

Harvey C. Jones, a former Synopsys CEO, became the company’s first board chair, leading its directors. The search for a permanent CEO included internal and external candidates. Nvidia kept its quarterly results scheduled for Nov. 17, followed by an earnings call at 5 p.m. Eastern.

title: Bitcoin Plunges, but Michael Saylor Says STRC Still Delivers Gains
summary: Michael Saylor highlighted positive returns from Strategy’s income-paying preferred shares, traded as STRC, while bitcoin fell near $64K on Nov. 14, down more than 21% over one month. The slide pushed the company’s bitcoin holdings further below their acquisition cost. Saylor Highlights Income Durin...
content:
Michael Saylor highlighted positive returns from Strategy’s income-paying preferred shares, traded as STRC, while bitcoin fell near $64K on Nov. 14, down more than 21% over one month. The slide pushed the company’s bitcoin holdings further below their acquisition cost.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin dropped more than 21% in one month, trading near $64K on Nov. 14.
  • Bitcoin lost 29.8% over one year in Saylor’s chart, while STRC returned 13.4%.
  • Near $64K, Strategy’s bitcoin sat more than $9 billion below its cost.

Saylor Highlights Income During Bitcoin’s Slide

Michael Saylor, founder and executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), compared STRC’s returns with bitcoin’s price performance on X on Nov. 14. STRC, also called Stretch, is its preferred stock with a dividend rate the company can adjust. The figures covered one week, one month, three months, and one year.

He outlined his digital credit model:

“Bitcoin is Digital Capital. Strategy transforms it into Digital Credit. Over the past month, bitcoin fell 17.3%. STRC’s price was essentially flat, and dividends brought its total return to +1.0%.”

The chart shows STRC returned 0.3% over one week and 13.4% over one year, while bitcoin fell 9.1% and 29.8%, respectively. Over three months, bitcoin gained 8.7%, exceeding STRC’s 7.5% return. The figures used data through 4 p.m. Eastern time on Nov. 13 and counted STRC dividends without assuming those payouts purchased more shares.

As of this writing, bitcoin traded at $64,428, down 5.85% over 24 hours, according to market data updated at 4:26 p.m. Eastern time on Nov. 14. Losses reached 14.37% over seven days, 21.21% over one month, and 32.22% over one year. The latest monthly decline exceeded the 17.3% drop in Saylor’s comparison, which used the previous day’s cutoff.

STRC’s 12% Rate Relies on Corporate Funding

Strategy’s STRC market metrics listed a $99.91 closing price on Nov. 13 and a 12% variable annualized dividend rate. At 12%, the dividend amounts to $12 a year per $100 stated amount per share if the rate remains unchanged.

Owning preferred shares creates a financial claim on the issuer, while direct bitcoin ownership gives the holder the cryptocurrency itself. STRC’s distributions depend on corporate funding, and its trading price can change independently of bitcoin.

Those funding requirements drew criticism from economist Peter Schiff, who questioned the assumptions behind STRC payments on Nov. 12, challenging expectations that long-term bitcoin appreciation could support the model. His criticism concerned payment sustainability, whereas Saylor’s latest chart measured historical investor returns.

Share Repurchases Continue as Bitcoin Holdings Lose Value

Common-stock sales financed the company’s latest bitcoin purchases and preferred-share repurchases. During Nov. 2-8, Strategy bought 1,036 BTC for $81.9 million. It also spent $188.3 million buying back 1,887,464 of its own STRC shares.

Meanwhile, Strategy’s bitcoin holdings fell further below their acquisition cost as the cryptocurrency declined. Valuing its disclosed 850,364 BTC at $64,428 produces approximately $54.79 billion, against a $64.16 billion purchase cost. That implies an unrealized loss of approximately $9.37 billion, based on its last reported holdings.

Separate dollar reserves and dividend funding supported the company’s payment obligations. As of Nov. 8, Strategy held a $4.77 billion designated dollar reserve, set aside for preferred-stock dividends and debt interest, alongside $146.2 million in separate cash. During Nov. 2-8, it used $21.1 million from the reserve to pay preferred-stock dividends.

title: Cobra Warns AI Threatens Bitcoin Self-Custody as Winter Looms
summary: The pseudonymous owner and maintainer of the bitcoin.org domain stated he had never seen bitcoiners so demoralized, highlighting that the recent bear market was brutal. Cobra pointed out several tailwinds for bitcoin’s future, stressing that owning bitcoin is extremely risky right now. Bitcoin.org S...
content:
The pseudonymous owner and maintainer of the bitcoin.org domain stated he had never seen bitcoiners so demoralized, highlighting that the recent bear market was brutal. Cobra pointed out several tailwinds for bitcoin’s future, stressing that owning bitcoin is extremely risky right now.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin.org maintainer Cobra warned of a brutal crypto winter due to AI threats and institutional dominance.
  • He cited rising cybersecurity risks, predicting increased self-custody breaches as AI outpaces defenses.
  • AI tech investments and geopolitical instability are draining capital away from an already risky bitcoin market.

Bitcoin.org Steward Cobra Highlights Tailwinds for Bitcoin in the Short Term

Cobra, the pseudonymous maintainer of the bitcoin.org domain, has laid out a bleak outlook for bitcoin’s future, outlining the difficulties the prime cryptocurrency faces.

Addressing the current state of the cryptocurrency market, Cobra said the recent price downtrend has been brutal for bitcoiners, who are demoralized and “barely hanging on,” as he noted on social media. Bitcoin has officially entered bear market territory, having recently lost nearly 20% of its value during the past 30 days

Cobra explained that with the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), owning bitcoin was full of risk and uncertainty, with holders remaining unrewarded for facing all that risk, disincentivizing bitcoin as an investment asset.

Cobra, who was concerned with self-custody issues for a long time, assessed that now, more than ever, self-custody had become a contentious point, as threat actors have a vast array of resources to attack security weaknesses in custody systems.

He alerted about a continued downtrend in bitcoin prices in October, stressing that the upcoming period would be the “most painful winter” given the current cybersecurity landscape as AI outpaces crypto defense systems. At the time, he assessed that many people would get drained and lose their BTC.

Similarly, he acknowledged that the market has been taken over by institutional investors such as Stratregy, with their massive stockpiles entailing their own problems, while retail investors were largely out of the market.

Cobra also stressed that Trump’s crypto allegiance will also affect regulatory aspects now that Democrats have taken control of the House and the Senate, and that the surge of colossal AI-linked initial public offerings (IPOs) will suck up capital otherwise directed to the crypto market, producing models that, at the same time, will affect bitcoin in “unpredictable ways” at some point.

“This and other factors like the Iran war and the AI bubble popping triggering a sell off make owning bitcoin extremely risky right now. OGs will be fine but people who got in recently are really in a bad place,” Cobra concluded.

Analysts like Peter Schiff have recently highlighted the drop in bitcoin prices, calling into question its viability as a store of value and recommending that crypto investors pivot to gold, even as its prices reach critical levels.

title: Unocoin Admits $200K Crypto Loss, Warns of Customer Data Breach
summary: Indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin confirmed Saturday, Nov. 14, that attackers stole approximately $200,000 in cryptocurrency from three compromised hot wallets, reversing its earlier assurances that no funds were lost. The trading platform’s team also acknowledged potential exposure of sensitiv...
content:
Indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin confirmed Saturday, Nov. 14, that attackers stole approximately $200,000 in cryptocurrency from three compromised hot wallets, reversing its earlier assurances that no funds were lost. The trading platform’s team also acknowledged potential exposure of sensitive customer information.

Key Takeaways

  • Unocoin confirmed approximately $200,000 in cryptocurrency losses across three of its more than 20 operational hot wallets.
  • Investigators determined that Unocoin-controlled backup signing keys were compromised, while Bitgo’s infrastructure remained unaffected.
  • Customer information may have been exposed, although Unocoin says it found no evidence that identity verification documents were accessed.

Unocoin’s $200K Revelation Rewrites Earlier Security Assurances

Unocoin’s Nov. 14 disclosure marks a significant departure from the company’s initial assessment following the Nov. 6 security incident. On Nov. 9, the Bengaluru-based exchange maintained that its intervention with custody providers had prevented cryptocurrency losses.

Subsequent forensic examinations, however, uncovered unauthorized transactions involving three operational hot wallets used for activities including customer withdrawals. The estimated $200,000 loss represents significantly less than 1% of cryptocurrency assets held on behalf of customers, according to Unocoin.

The exchange pledged to absorb the financial damage rather than impose losses on account holders. “Unocoin will fully fund the identified loss from its own resources,” the company stated, adding that affected cryptocurrency balances would not be reduced.

Unocoin also reported successfully freezing a portion of the affected funds through coordination with industry partners, although it did not disclose the amount recovered or restricted.

Eight-Year-Old Backup Keys Emerge as Critical Vulnerability

Perhaps the investigation’s most consequential finding concerns encrypted backup signing keys generated approximately eight years ago, printed on paper, and placed in secure physical storage. Investigators determined that these Unocoin-controlled keys were compromised and subsequently used to authorize unauthorized cryptocurrency transfers.

The exchange acknowledged that investigators have yet to establish precisely how the keys were accessed, despite identifying a decryption passphrase within compromised infrastructure. The findings also reinforce Bitgo’s Nov. 13 explanation that its custody systems were never breached.

Under Unocoin’s two-of-three multisignature arrangement, the exchange controlled two signing keys, allowing transactions to be authorized without Bitgo’s participation. The custodian previously explained that the suspicious transactions were signed using Unocoin’s user and backup keys before being broadcast independently to blockchain networks.

Customer Data Exposure Raises Additional Questions

Beyond the cryptocurrency theft, Unocoin acknowledged that portions of its infrastructure may have exposed registered email addresses, residential addresses, encrypted passwords, account balances, and know-your-customer (KYC) information.

However, the company emphasized that investigators have not identified evidence of unauthorized access to actual identity verification documents. Customers were warned about targeted phishing attempts exploiting potentially compromised personal information.

Meanwhile, Unocoin continues rebuilding its infrastructure, conducting security audits, and investigating the circumstances surrounding the compromised signing keys before restoring services.

The exchange’s latest admission resolves the immediate question of whether cryptocurrency was stolen, but leaves important uncertainties surrounding data exposure, key security, and operational recovery. Its promise to reimburse customers addresses the financial shortfall, while the unresolved method of compromise presents a more complicated challenge to restoring confidence.

  • CMC sets that grey price itself, from the expected listing price instead of trades in private shares.

CMC Markets has started selling UK clients options tied to Anthropic's expected share price before the artificial intelligence company lists, it said today (Saturday). CMC described itself as the first UK-regulated broker to offer options on pre-IPO grey markets.

Clients can buy calls and puts, and the premium paid is the most they can lose, according to CMC. The pre-IPO contracts other brokers opened on Anthropic in recent weeks are leveraged contracts for difference, priced two different ways at ThinkMarkets and Pepperstone.

Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq listing on October 26. Since then, the race to sell UK retail investors some form of exposure has drawn brokers, a crypto exchange and the company's own share offer.

London's trading industry is coming home!

How the Options Settle

The options are European-style and cash-settled. If Anthropic lists before an option expires, the contract settles against the official closing price of the listed shares, CMC said. If it has not listed, settlement uses the grey market price.

The product builds on the grey market spread bets and CFDs CMC first offered on SpaceX in May, which are leveraged and roll into ordinary share positions once a company trades. CMC clients traded an estimated $451 billion a month over the two quarters to September, FM Intelligence's broker volumes data show.

Laurence Booth, global head of markets at CMC Markets, presented the options as a way into companies that retail clients usually cannot reach before a listing.

"It significantly broadens the range of opportunities available," Booth said.

When it launched SpaceX trading, CMC had not said how it would set the grey market price. Its website now says CMC sets it from its own view of the expected listing price, using the indicative price range where one exists, valuations of comparable listed companies and market sentiment.

The price is not based on trades in private shares, and with no exchange-traded reference before a listing, the product cannot be hedged in the open market, according to the same page. Option prices add an estimate of future volatility on top.

What Each Route Gives a Retail Client

Brokers and exchanges now sell UK retail investors at least four kinds of exposure to the same listing, and they differ in what the client ends up holding.

ThinkMarkets quotes Anthropic's value at the end of its first trading day, while Pepperstone tracks the expected opening share price. Both are leveraged CFDs, the category in which European regulators have also placed perpetual futures.

Kraken lets eligible clients request share-backed ANTx tokens, The Defiant reported this week, with no allocation guaranteed. For the shares themselves, Anthropic has named six UK platforms for a retail offer coordinated by RetailBook, a list that does not include Robinhood.

Of the four, the share offer and the tokens give the client a claim on stock. CMC's options are the only one of the derivatives where the maximum loss is known when the trade opens.

CMC said the options are available to UK clients from Saturday, with a broader global rollout planned. Clients must pass an appropriateness assessment for both OTC options and grey market products, according to its website.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen With 2.5x Faster Performance, Challenging GPT-6.1 and Claude
summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more efficient AI model designed to compete with frontier systems while expanding its presence across search, coding, and agentic workflows.
content:
Skip to content

Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more efficient AI model designed to compete with frontier systems while expanding its presence across search, coding, and agentic workflows.

Announced on November 12, the model brings a reported 2.5x improvement in task completion speed over Gemini 3.8 Flash, alongside stronger coding capabilities and lower execution costs. Google is positioning Hydrogen as an accessible option for developers and businesses that need fast AI execution without relying on its more computationally intensive models.

Google announced the global rollout of Gemini 4 Hydrogen, upgrading Search’s intent recognition to better understand complex, nuanced queries, including typos and natural language. Source: Google via X

The release also marks a significant expansion of Google’s Gemini 4 ecosystem, with the model becoming available across Google Search, the Gemini app, AI Studio, and developer platforms. Its benchmark results place it ahead of GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in several categories, although competitors retain advantages in other specialized tasks.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Targets Faster AI Coding and Agentic Workflows

Google DeepMind designed Gemini 4 Hydrogen to handle everyday coding, software development, multimodal tasks, and agentic workflows with greater execution speed. Unlike Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, which focus on complex reasoning and longer tasks, Hydrogen prioritizes rapid execution and efficiency.

Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a fast, efficient model for everyday coding, agentic workflows, and rapid execution, complementing Gemini 4 Carbon’s advanced reasoning capabilities. Source: Google AI via X

According to Google, Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at its default high thinking setting. The company also reported that its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score increased to 57%, compared with 18.2% for its predecessor.

The improvement extends beyond processing speed. Google said Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than five times and handles unsuccessful tool calls or empty search results more effectively. These capabilities are particularly relevant to autonomous AI agents, which must navigate multiple steps, use external tools, and recover from errors without constant human intervention.

The model also introduces four configurable thinking levels, including a new xhigh setting. Users can adjust the reasoning effort according to the complexity of their tasks, balancing response speed against the resources required for more demanding work.

Google DeepMind said Hydrogen also surpassed Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Intelligence Index at its default high setting, scoring 51 against Argon’s 50. Its score rises to 54 when using the highest xhigh setting.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Challenges GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5

Google’s published benchmark evaluations show that Gemini 4 Hydrogen can compete with established frontier models across coding, reasoning, and professional workflows.

In the SWE-sweep evaluation, which measures an AI model’s ability to identify and repair software issues, Hydrogen scored 13.5%. This exceeded Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 3.1% and GPT-6.1 Terra at 5.8%.

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a faster upgrade over Gemini 3.8 Flash, optimized for coding, multimodal tasks, agentic workflows, and everyday use. Source: @GoogleDeepMind via X

Hydrogen also recorded a 71.6% score on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1, ahead of GPT-6.1 Terra at 69.8% and Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 60.4%. The benchmark evaluates how effectively AI systems complete complex professional tasks involving multiple steps and different forms of information.

Its HLE-Diamond score reached 58.8%, compared with 53.3% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and 47.3% for GPT-6.1 Terra. On AutomationBench-AA, Hydrogen achieved 76.1%, outperforming both competitors in the published comparison.

However, the results do not establish an across-the-board advantage. Claude Sonnet 5.5 scored 63.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, above Hydrogen’s 57%. Claude also led the OSWorld-2.1 computer-use evaluation with 83.9%, compared with Hydrogen’s 77.6%.

Google’s evaluation methodology combines its own testing with results reported by competing model providers and public benchmark leaderboards. The company also used different testing configurations across evaluations, making individual benchmark results more useful than treating the overall comparison as a definitive ranking.

Nevertheless, the results demonstrate Google’s progress in making a faster model competitive across several demanding AI applications.

Independent Tests Highlight Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s Cost Advantage

Early demonstrations from independent developers have also drawn attention to Hydrogen’s execution speed and operating costs.

In one comparison shared by developer @EnvolDev, Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon were assigned the same complex task through OpenRouter using the High setting. Hydrogen completed the task in 1 hour and 23 minutes at a reported cost of $4.27.

A split-screen video compares Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Carbon generating an arctic boat scene, highlighting Hydrogen’s faster execution and lower cost. Source: @EnvolDev/X

Gemini 4 Carbon took 2 hours and 39 minutes and cost $8.83 to complete the same task. The side-by-side demonstration showed both models generating an arctic boat scene with ice formations and marine elements.

Although this was an individual test rather than a standardized benchmark, the results highlight the potential cost and time advantages of using Hydrogen for workloads that do not require the deeper reasoning capabilities of Carbon.

A separate demonstration shared by @AI_Screening compared Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Carbon, and Argon in AI video generation. The models generated a stylized horse galloping across a savanna at sunset, allowing viewers to compare motion quality, environmental effects, and visual consistency.

Hydrogen delivered competitive animation quality in the demonstration while offering faster generation and lower costs. These results suggest that the model could provide an efficient option for certain multimodal creative workflows, although individual demonstrations do not establish consistent performance across different prompts and generation tasks.

Google Upgrades Search With Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Alongside the model launch, Google has introduced a significant upgrade to Google Search, integrating Gemini 4 Hydrogen to improve how the platform understands and responds to complicated queries.

The November 12 rollout allows Search to interpret more nuanced, multi-part questions, including requests written in natural language or containing difficult-to-understand typos. The system is designed to identify the user’s intent more accurately rather than relying solely on individual keywords.

Google has also improved its query fan-out capabilities. The technology allows Search to explore several related subtopics simultaneously, connecting users with a wider selection of relevant websites and information sources.

The updated experience introduces more adaptive visual responses, including images, comparison tables, structured information, and custom tools. These features are intended to make complicated searches easier to understand without requiring users to navigate multiple pages manually.

Robby Stein, Google’s vice president of product for Search, described the release as the biggest model upgrade to Search yet. He said the update would help users find relevant information through more intuitive and visually structured responses.

Google also highlighted improvements to language understanding across supported AI Mode languages, extending the upgraded search experience to users making queries in different languages.

The integration is particularly important for Google’s broader AI strategy because it brings Gemini’s reasoning and information-processing capabilities directly into one of the company’s most widely used products.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Expands Across Google’s AI Ecosystem

Google is making Gemini 4 Hydrogen available across its consumer, developer, and enterprise platforms, increasing access to its latest AI capabilities.

Developers can use the model through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Android Studio. Businesses can also access it through Gemini for business and supported enterprise tools, while general users can find Hydrogen in the Gemini app and Google Search.

A split-screen comparison evaluates Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Carbon (Medium), and Argon in generating a galloping horse scene, highlighting differences in motion quality, dust effects, and visual consistency. Source: @AI_Screening/X

Google is also introducing a multi-model approach through its Antigravity development platform. Its Orchestrator feature can dynamically switch between Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen during a single session, assigning more complex reasoning tasks to Carbon and faster execution work to Hydrogen.

According to Google, this approach achieved near-Carbon task success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster on average.

The model’s API pricing is set at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across its one-million-token context window. This gives developers a defined cost structure when integrating Hydrogen into applications and automated workflows.

By combining configurable reasoning, faster execution, and multi-model coordination, Google is targeting users who need to manage increasingly complex AI workloads without relying exclusively on its most resource-intensive systems.

Google’s AI Competition Intensifies

The launch of Gemini 4 Hydrogen strengthens Google’s position in an increasingly competitive AI market, where model performance is no longer measured solely by reasoning capabilities.

Speed, inference costs, coding accuracy, and the ability to complete multi-step tasks have become important factors for developers and businesses choosing AI systems. Google’s latest release addresses these requirements while extending its Gemini technology into Search and everyday productivity tools.

Its benchmark performance against GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 provides evidence of progress in several categories, although differences in computer use and terminal-based tasks show that competitors remain competitive.

The introduction of Hydrogen also reflects a broader shift toward specialized AI models that can handle routine execution more efficiently while working alongside larger systems for demanding reasoning tasks.

As Google expands access to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its ability to maintain benchmark performance while delivering measurable savings in execution time and costs will be an important factor in determining its adoption among developers, enterprises, and everyday users.

title: Fed Rate Hike Odds Reach Near-Certainty as Bitcoin Price Falls to $65K
summary: Federal Reserve interest rate expectations have taken a decidedly hawkish turn, with CME Fedwatch assigning a near-guaranteed probability to a December rate increase on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. Kalshi and Polymarket traders largely agree, while bitcoin has slipped to an intraday low of $65,020. CME ...
content:
Federal Reserve interest rate expectations have taken a decidedly hawkish turn, with CME Fedwatch assigning a near-guaranteed probability to a December rate increase on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. Kalshi and Polymarket traders largely agree, while bitcoin has slipped to an intraday low of $65,020.

Key Takeaways

  • CME Fedwatch assigns an 88.5% probability to a quarter-point December hike and 11.5% to a half-point increase.
  • Kalshi and Polymarket favor a 25-basis-point hike, with probabilities of 89% and 88%, respectively.
  • Bitcoin touched $65,020 on Bitstamp on Saturday morning as inflation concerns and expectations of tighter monetary policy weighed on risk assets.

CME Fedwatch Signals December Hike as Prediction Markets Follow

According to the CME Fedwatch tool and data Bitcoin.com News reviewed Saturday morning, futures traders assign an 88.5% probability to the Federal Reserve lifting its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points at its Dec. 8-9 meeting. Another 11.5% favors a more aggressive 50-basis-point increase, leaving no probability assigned to unchanged rates or cuts.

The current federal funds target range stands at 3.75% to 4%. A quarter-point increase would raise that range to 4%-4.25%, while a half-point adjustment would place borrowing costs between 4.25% and 4.5%.

Expectations have changed considerably. On Nov. 6, CME assigned a 23.7% probability to unchanged rates and 76.3% to a quarter-point increase. By Saturday, the possibility of a half-point move had entered the equation at 11.5%.

Meanwhile, Kalshi traders priced a 25-basis-point hike at 89%, compared with 10% for a larger increase. The platform recorded approximately $14.3 million in trading volume on its December decision market.

On Polymarket, the corresponding probabilities stood at 88% and approximately 9%, respectively, with cumulative volume exceeding $33.7 million. Both prediction platforms retained roughly 4% probabilities for unchanged rates, unlike CME’s futures-derived calculations.

These figures represent market expectations rather than confirmed monetary policy, but typically, the market is correct. The Federal Open Market Committee has not announced its December decision, and the three platforms use different pricing methodologies and contract specifications. There’s still a considerable amount of time left until the Fed makes the year-end move.

Why Are Federal Reserve Rate Hike Odds Climbing?

Inflation has become a central concern. October’s consumer price index increased 0.4%, exceeding economists’ 0.3% forecast, while core inflation advanced 0.3%, also surpassing expectations. Persistent price pressures have strengthened arguments for additional monetary tightening.

Energy costs have complicated the outlook. Brent crude’s advance beyond $100 per barrel and elevated diesel prices have increased transportation expenses, potentially spreading massive price pressures into food, services, and consumer goods.

The labor market has also complicated the case for restraint. October payrolls in the U.S. increased by 165,000, comfortably exceeding expectations near 65,000. Stronger employment figures give policymakers additional room to consider higher borrowing costs.

Federal Reserve Gov. Christopher Waller has advocated additional tightening and raised the possibility of a half-point increase if underlying inflation remained elevated. Other officials have expressed concerns about persistent price pressures, although the appropriate pace of tightening remains contested.

Bitcoin Tests $65,000 as Monetary Pressure Intensifies

Bitcoin’s price deterioration offers another indication of mounting anxiety across speculative markets. Bitstamp’s 30-minute chart showed the cryptocurrency retreating from $72,128 to $65,020 before recovering modestly to $65,274 around 11:14 a.m. EST.

The chart above displays successive lower highs and lower lows, accompanied by elevated selling volume. Immediate support sits near $65,000, while $66,000 represents the first significant resistance threshold. A sustained breakdown could expose the $64,500-$64,000 region. Today’s intraday low of $65,020 per bitcoin brought $1 billion in 24-hour liquidations across the entire crypto market, with $382 million being BTC wipeouts.

Higher interest rates can diminish the appeal of speculative assets by increasing financing costs and making interest-bearing alternatives more attractive. Nevertheless, bitcoin’s decline cannot be attributed exclusively to Federal Reserve expectations. A lot of other factors have come into play, including uncertainty surrounding Strategy’s MSCI index listing and exchange-traded fund (ETF) outflows.

With the December decision approaching, investors face an increasingly uncomfortable proposition: Inflation remains stubborn, monetary policy could tighten further, and bitcoin is struggling to establish a convincing floor. Markets have largely settled on a December hike, but its magnitude and consequences remain unresolved.

title: AI Agents Can Now Buy Computing With Bitcoin—Does Lightning Have Its Use Case?
summary: Lightning Labs’ pi402 lets coding agents pay for AI inference with Bitcoin. The launch tests whether tiny automated payments can solve a real computing business problem.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Lightning Labs’ pi402 lets coding agents pay for AI inference with Bitcoin. The launch tests whether tiny automated payments can solve a real computing business problem.

AI agents have a new way to spend Bitcoin: buying the computing needed to keep working. Lightning Labs has launched pi402, a tool that lets coding agents pay for AI inference over the Lightning Network.

The November 12 announcement moves the agent-payments debate toward a specific purchase. Rather than imagining software shopping autonomously for everything, it starts with a recurring need: access to an AI model that can process the next prompt.

“Inference is the fuel every agent runs on,” Lightning Labs’ Olaoluwa Osuntokun wrote. The business question is whether a Bitcoin payment can make that fuel easier to buy and sell.

How AI agents use Bitcoin for inference

Pi402 connects the Pi coding-agent environment with paid inference services. The launch describes an embedded Wavelength wallet and controls for per-request spending and daily budgets. A human still funds the wallet and sets the operating boundaries.

The attraction is access without creating a separate buyer account or supplying a card to each participating seller. That does not make the entire AI service anonymous, unregulated or free of provider conditions. It changes the payment and access mechanism for services that implement it.

According to the L402 documentation, a buyer first requests a protected resource. The server returns a payment-required response, a credential and a Lightning invoice. Paying produces proof that can be presented with the credential to gain access.

The payment becomes part of authorisation rather than an invoice to settle later. The documentation also describes restricting and delegating bearer credentials, which matters when one piece of software needs to give another a limited ability to buy or access resources.

The useful detail is metering, not a payment for every word

The Aperture v0.6.0 release notes describe prepaid bundles that are drawn down according to actual usage. A single Lightning payment can therefore support multiple model requests. The system does not need to initiate a separate payment for every generated token.

The proxy obtains a price, reserves an estimated amount for a request and accounts for the reported usage afterward. When the remaining balance cannot cover another request, it can issue a new payment challenge.

That distinction separates a plausible billing system from a flashy demonstration. Model responses vary in length. Sellers need a way to price that uncertainty, and buyers need to see what they have actually consumed.

The same release supports both L402 and the Payment HTTP Authentication Scheme used by the Machine Payments Protocol. Supporting more than one payment-authentication format could help services meet different clients, although compatibility by itself does not establish commercial adoption.

The seller still has costs, accounts and exchange-rate exposure

Lightning Labs’ public Lightmeter repository shows another important layer. It converts a provider’s dollar-denominated model prices into millisatoshis per token, can add a seller margin and reconciles usage against the provider’s billing records.

A millisatoshi is one-thousandth of a satoshi. That granularity allows small accounting units, but the conversion does not make the underlying computing free or ensure that Bitcoin-denominated prices stay constant.

The repository’s architecture places the upstream provider’s API key at the proxy. In other words, removing an API key from the buyer’s experience does not necessarily remove API keys from the supply chain. Someone still needs to secure the provider relationship and pay its bill.

That gives the story a more grounded commercial angle. A reseller could offer a narrow, paid entry point to computing while managing procurement and billing behind it. Whether that arrangement is attractive depends on price, reliability, model access and the terms of the upstream service.

Why irreversible payments are a trade-off

Osuntokun argues that card chargebacks are poorly matched to computing that has already been consumed. A completed response cannot be ungenerated so that a seller can recover the electricity and GPU time.

Final payment can reduce that particular uncertainty for a seller. For a buyer, however, it raises the importance of spending controls and service quality. Paying successfully establishes access; it does not prove that an answer is correct or that an autonomous workflow was worth its cost.

BNC’s coverage of Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 examined falling model prices alongside the continuing need for human judgment. Automating payment makes that distinction more consequential: a system can spend efficiently while pursuing an unhelpful task.

The adoption test starts with something measurable

The launch supplies software and an identifiable use case, rather than evidence that a large new market already exists. The announcement does not establish independent transaction volume, recurring demand or a broad network of competing sellers.

Useful follow-up evidence would include repeat purchases, the number of active providers, total payment costs and how often spending limits prevent unwanted work. Those measures would help distinguish a convenient developer tool from a meaningful new source of Lightning usage.

For Bitcoin, the opportunity is straightforward: a machine-native service being bought through a machine-readable payment. Pi402 makes that proposition testable. Its success will depend on whether developers keep choosing it after the novelty of an agent with a wallet has worn off.

title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
Bitcoin price crashed about 13% over the past week and traded near $65,600 on Saturday.
This post Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low first appeared o...
content:
Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike.

A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning.

A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900.

Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough.

A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price

The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes.

Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show.

Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down.

ETF outflows continue as mining difficulty drops

Demand from spot bitcoin ETFs has not filled the gap. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows through Wednesday, and the funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday. Weekend trading is typically thinner, leaving the bitcoin price more exposed to sharp swings in either direction.

Miners got some relief overnight. Bitcoin’s mining difficulty dropped 9.13% at 12:02 a.m. ET Saturday at block 975,744, falling from about 148.36 trillion to 134.82 trillion, the largest cut since June. Difficulty adjusts automatically every 2,016 blocks to keep average block times near 10 minutes.

The next tests for the bitcoin price arrive quickly. Traders will watch whether Saturday’s slide holds below Friday’s $67,555 low, and whether Nvidia’s report on Tuesday extends the chip-stock weakness that has followed bitcoin lower all week. With a December rate hike fully priced and the dollar at a 19-month high, any further jump in yields when markets reopen could keep pressure on.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $65,100.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: XRP Price Today: $0.98 Support Under Threat Despite Oversold RSI
summary: XRP fell below the $1 psychological threshold on November 14, trading near $0.98 as persistent selling pressure pushed the cryptocurrency to multi-month lows.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP fell below the $1 psychological threshold on November 14, trading near $0.98 as persistent selling pressure pushed the cryptocurrency to multi-month lows.

Deeply oversold indicators suggest a possible relief bounce, but the broader technical structure remains bearish.

The XRP price has declined approximately 4% over 24 hours, 15% over the past week, and more than 25% over the past month. The latest correction has placed the $0.98–$0.99 region under pressure, raising concerns about whether buyers can prevent another move toward $0.80.

Bears Test $0.98–$0.99 Critical Support

XRP was trading between approximately $0.982 and $0.986 on November 14, following a decline that briefly pushed the asset below $1. The weakness reflects broader pressure across the cryptocurrency market, alongside a deterioration in XRP’s technical structure.

XRP failed to break $1.55 resistance, reversing from recent highs toward the channel’s lower boundary near $0.99. Source: Ali Martinez/X

In a three-day chart analysis, crypto analyst Ali Charts identified approximately $0.99 as the lower boundary of an established trading channel. XRP had previously failed to overcome resistance near $1.55 before reversing toward this level.

The analyst warned that losing $0.99 could expose the cryptocurrency to further losses toward $0.80. For an initial recovery, XRP needs to reclaim $1 and move above the $1.02 pivot region, with immediate resistance around $1.04 and $1.06.

XRP Technical Indicators Signal Strong Selling Pressure

XRP’s moving averages continue to reflect a strong bearish trend. Multi-timeframe readings show the cryptocurrency trading below its short-, medium-, and long-term simple and exponential moving averages.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The 10-period averages are positioned around $1.08–$1.09, while the 20-period readings sit near $1.16–$1.18. Longer-term averages are considerably higher, with the 50-period indicators around $1.26–$1.32 and the 200-period readings near $1.26–$1.34.

This positioning highlights the distance XRP must recover before challenging its previous trading levels.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains negative near -0.08, with its signal line around -0.06. Its negative histogram indicates that bearish momentum has not yet produced a confirmed reversal. The Average Directional Index (ADX) also points to a relatively strong directional trend on several timeframes.

Together, these readings show that the prevailing downtrend remains established, despite signs of extreme selling conditions in shorter-term oscillators.

Oversold RSI Raises the Possibility of an XRP Rebound

The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) is hovering around 19.8–20.8, considerably below the conventional 30 threshold for oversold conditions. Other oscillators show similar extremes, with Stochastic %K near 3–5, the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) around -130 to -143, and Williams %R near -98 to -99.

These readings indicate that XRP has experienced intense selling pressure. They also raise the possibility of short-term consolidation or a technical rebound if buyers begin entering the market.

However, oversold conditions do not guarantee a price recovery. An asset can remain in this territory during an extended downtrend, particularly when broader market sentiment remains weak.

A sustained recovery above the $1.02 pivot, accompanied by improving momentum, would provide more convincing evidence that selling pressure is easing. Until then, the RSI readings alone are insufficient to establish a bullish reversal.

Coinbase XRP Buying Activity Offers a Contrasting Signal

Despite the broader decline, exchange-flow data has revealed a potentially important development in XRP’s market structure.

Crypto analyst CW8900 reported that Coinbase shifted to net XRP buying over two consecutive days after recording substantial initial selling activity that coincided with the recent price decline.

The volume of net selling on Coinbase was significantly higher than that seen on Binance or OKX during the decline. Source: @CW8900/X

The analyst’s exchange-flow comparison examined price movements, trading volume, and cumulative netflow or delta readings across Coinbase, Binance, Bitfinex, and OKX.

The data highlighted significant volatility around November 13, when selling pressure and leveraged liquidations contributed to XRP’s downward movement.

Coinbase’s subsequent shift toward net buying is notable because the exchange had previously recorded comparatively heavy net selling. The change suggests that buying activity emerged even as XRP remained under pressure.

The analyst also highlighted whale activity and high-leverage liquidations during the decline. The resulting accumulation signals indicate that some market participants were willing to acquire XRP at lower prices despite the market’s weakness.

However, net buying on a single exchange does not establish that the broader market has entered an accumulation phase. It also does not confirm that XRP has reached a price bottom.

Nevertheless, the development offers a contrasting perspective to the bearish technical indicators and suggests that buying interest has not disappeared entirely.

XRP Price Prediction: $0.75 Support and $10 Long-Term Projection

A separate monthly XRP chart analysis identifies a broader ascending channel that could influence the cryptocurrency’s longer-term direction.

According to the analysis, the price remains within a rising channel, with its lower trendline serving as an important structural support. The $0.75 region is highlighted as a critical level for preserving this formation.

XRP maintains a broader ascending channel, with $0.75 serving as critical support for preserving its bullish structure; a breakdown could trigger a deeper correction. Source: TradingView

A sustained hold above $0.75 would keep the ascending-channel structure intact, while a confirmed breakdown could indicate a deeper correction and deteriorating long-term sentiment.

The monthly RSI currently stands near 41, below its neutral midpoint of 50. This indicates weakening momentum, although it does not represent the extreme oversold conditions observed on the daily timeframe. A recovery above 50 would suggest improving longer-term buying momentum.

The analyst also outlined a potential long-term upside projection toward $10, based on the channel’s upper boundary. However, this remains a technical scenario rather than a confirmed price target. XRP would first need to stabilize, overcome intermediate resistance levels, and demonstrate sustained momentum improvement.

For now, the market presents conflicting signals. Bearish trend indicators point to continued pressure, while deeply oversold oscillators and Coinbase’s recent buying activity suggest that a short-term recovery remains possible. The coming price action will help determine whether XRP can stabilize or extend its correction.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, MegaETH co-founder Shuyao Kong said the restructuring affected employees who helped build the project’s blockchain, wallet and ecosystem. OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, while Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake.

MegaETH parent cuts 20% of staff amid restructuring, AI push

MEGA, the organization behind Ethereum layer-2 network MegaETH, has reduced its workforce by 20% following months of restructuring as it expands into artificial intelligence products. 

On Friday, MegaETH co-founder Shuyao Kong said the organization had reorganized its teams, resulting in the departures of staff who worked on its blockchain, wallet, ecosystem support and communications. Kong did not disclose the number of employees affected or when the layoffs occurred. She said MEGA’s founders, early employees and core engineering team remain committed to the organization.

“We’ve brought together new capabilities and reorganized our teams, a process that has resulted in a 20% reduction in our staff,” Kong said. “These are people who helped build MEGA from its earliest days.”

The workforce reduction comes as MEGA shifts its focus toward developing products on the MegaETH network, including artificial intelligence services. The organization has committed $30 million to the initiative, although Kong did not directly link the layoffs to its new strategy.

In a whitepaper, MegaETH co-founders Yilong Li and Lei Yang outlined a proposed inference market aimed at giving users access to competing AI service providers. Their approach seeks to address concerns about whether providers use the advertised models and how they handle customer data.

Kong said MEGA plans to launch a public inference market in December.

OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex

OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa.

The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said.

The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction.

The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems.

Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT

Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%.

The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings.

Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million.

Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday.

The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million).

title: Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack

content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 14, 2026

Microsoft attributed the outage to a network capacity upgrade issue, confirming that the disruption was unrelated to cyberattacks or AI agents.

Microsoft said it restored Microsoft 365 services after a global outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other applications for more than 24 hours, reiterating that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.

On Saturday, the company said it “restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” directing customers to incident MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

On Friday, Microsoft said that the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that emerged after a recent network change. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents,” the company said.

The company said it addressed the underlying issue and restored services gradually, checking stability before proceeding to the next stage. Microsoft apologized for the disruption and said it would publish a full post-incident report once its review is complete.

The outage began Thursday, disrupting access to Exchange Online mailboxes and features linked to Outlook, Teams and Microsoft Copilot. Government agencies in Japan, Singapore and the United States experienced email problems, while connections between Microsoft 365 and AI assistants were also affected.

OpenAI said the Microsoft 365 connector in ChatGPT was operating normally again, while Anthropic also marked its Microsoft 365 connector and Claude for Outlook incident as resolved.
